messages:
sam_support: FYI ACME (acme-corp) opened a ticket — users reporting 403 on /console and 403 when calling model endpoints. Happened right after the RBAC policy tiering rollout this morning. They can authenticate but get forbidden.

acme_ops: Confirmed. Browser shows 403 on /models and billing pages. Token scopes look normal from client side. Login via SSO works.

sam_support: Noted. tagging @raj_sec and @elaine_sre. Any quick checks we should run?

raj_sec: First guess is attribute-based role mapping drift from the new tiering policy. Can you paste the user id (subject) for a blocked user?

acme_ops: user: alice@acme.com. Also sending a service_account call that fails with request id r-7f4b2.

elaine_sre: Run the rolesync check and policy eval on that principal:

```bash
rbacctl evaluate --tenant acme-corp --principal "user:alice@acme.com" --resource "models:read"
```

sam_support: Ran it, output below:
```
rolesync: ok
eval: DENY (missing attribute: org_tier=enterprise)
```

kim_eng: ah — the rollout added a required org_tier attribute for model and billing scopes. Looks like ACME's org attribute didn't sync from IdP after the upgrade. Could be a rolesync webhook failure.

rolesync-bot: rolesync job `rolesync.acme-corp` failed at 14:05 UTC with 502 from idp.acme.com, retrying. Last successful sync: 2025-11-01T02:48:12Z.

raj_sec: That matches. Two action paths: 1) provide a temporary policy grant to restore access immediately, or 2) fix rolesync upstream and let the attribute flow restore permissions. For customers on paid tier we usually do (1) + (2).

sam_support: Customer asked for immediate access. What's the exact temporary policy command?

kim_eng: Use the grant API to attach a fallback role that maps to the previous permission set (pre-tiering). Example:

```bash
redwoodctl grants create --tenant acme-corp --principal "group:admins@acme.com" --role "legacy-admin-fallback" --expiry 24h --reason "emergency restore due to rolesync drift"
```

elaine_sre: I applied a 6h fallback grant to group:admins@acme.com for acme-corp (grant id g-2a9c). Please verify.

acme_ops: Verified — models page and billing returned for Alice. :white_check_mark: Thank you.

raj_sec: Good. Next: we need a root cause for rolesync failure. Kim, can you check the rolesync logs and the webhook delivery errors?

kim_eng: Investigating. Found retries for payload to idp.acme.com returning 502 every 30s between 14:04–14:12. IdP reported a transient config rollback during their maintenance window. We'll add a warning and automatic backoff for future rollouts.

sam_support: I'll update the ticket with timeline and the temporary grant id + expiry. Also mention recommended permanent fix (ensure org_tier attribute present in IdP mapping).

raj_sec: One compliance note — because we created a temporary fallback grant we need an audit entry and postmortem: include who requested (sam_support), who approved (raj_sec), grant id, and which principals were affected. Also make sure key rotation/KMS ops weren't involved here. This is purely attributesync.

elaine_sre: Added audit entry: audit-9876 with details. I also scheduled a follow-up to revoke any lingering grants and to run a verification script across top 10 tenants that use tiered policies.

acme_ops: Thanks team. Can you send the confirmation email to our security contact when you close? They want the timeline and evidence that access was restored via fallback + root cause.

sam_support: Will do. Closing notes: rollback window for the tiering rollout set to 14:00–15:00 UTC; we applied fallback at 14:20 and verified restore at 14:23. Rolesync failure from IdP caused attribute drift; resolved by IdP at ~14:40, we kept fallback until IdP stable then revoked at 20:25 per policy.

acme_ops: Received, closing ticket now. :thumbsup:
